judge_panel.reason: The paper states GP-MILP 'preserv[es] MILP-equivalent solutions on the evaluated dataset, i.e., yielding the same objective value and connectivity outcome as the MILP solved on the complete graphs,' but reports no failure counts, objective-gap distribution, or formal sufficient condition for when pruning at Thr=0.15 guarantees retention of all optimal edges, leaving the claim unsubstantiated beyond an empirical assertion.

The paper claims, "GP-MILP execution times stay below 30 ms for nearly all graph instances, while preserving MILP-equivalent solutions on the evaluated dataset, i.e., yielding the same objective value and connectivity outcome as the MILP solved on the complete graphs." But the only accompanying table is "TABLE II: Percentage of graph instances meeting given latency thresholds," so the paper does not provide failure counts, objective-gap distributions, or conditions guaranteeing that pruning preserves the optimum.

The authors state that GP-MILP preserves MILP-equivalent solutions ("yielding the same objective value and connectivity outcome"), but given a reported edge recall of 99%, the paper does not quantify how often pruning drops critical links or report failure counts/gap distributions for when the optimum is missed.
